Appendix.description: Section 11: payloads, audit, scope events, FP log, glossary.
Appendix.title: Appendix

AttackPathEntry.description: A composed path: its hops, what it achieves, and the cheapest way to break it.
AttackPathEntry.title: AttackPathEntry

AttackPathHop.description:
One hop of a chain as the report renders it (REQ-AGENT-003).

``verified`` is the load-bearing field: a hop the analyzer accepted is evidence, and one it
did not is a *candidate* that names the check which would verify it. A report that showed
both the same way would be claiming a chain it cannot support.
AttackPathHop.title: AttackPathHop

AuditHighlights.description: The audit-log summary and out-of-scope events (appendix B/C).
AuditHighlights.title: AuditHighlights

Branding.description:
White-label presentation for a report (S14, MSSP use case).

The default is the neutral ARACHNE presentation, so a report rendered with no branding
is byte-identical to the pre-S14 output (the renderers only add a block when
:meth:`is_customised`). A project stores its branding as YAML/JSON; every value here is
operator-supplied, so colours and the logo URL are validated at construction rather
than escaped downstream.

``logo_url`` is **HTML/PDF only** and must be ``https``/``http``/``data:image`` — the
Markdown renderer prints ``logo_text`` (initials) instead, because Markdown has no
dependable way to carry a remote image into a text report. ``classification`` is the
handling banner (``CONFIDENTIAL``, ``INTERNAL``); it is printed on every page footer.
Branding.title: Branding

CheckRun.description: One check that ran (or was deliberately not run) — scope & methodology section.
CheckRun.title: CheckRun

Classification.description: CWE/CVE/CAPEC and the OWASP Top-10 mapping (``classification``).
Classification.title: Classification

ControlCoverage.description:
One framework control as this scan assessed it (S22, REQ-TRUST-001).

``status`` is deliberately one of ``pass``/``fail``/``gap`` and nothing else:
there is no "compliant". A control whose checks found nothing *passed this
scan's checks*; one whose checks did not run is a ``gap`` naming why — an
unassessed control must never read as a clean one.
ControlCoverage.title: ControlCoverage

DetectionAction.description:
One purple-team test artifact a scan emitted (S24, area VALID).

``nonce`` is the run's visible tag: it appears in every payload the action sent and in
every artifact the scan recorded, which is what makes "the defender saw *this* test" a
decidable question rather than a correlation guess (REQ-VALID-003).
DetectionAction.title: DetectionAction

DetectionValidation.description:
The purple-team half of a scan report (S24, REQ-VALID-003/004).

Present only for a purple-team run: an ordinary scan's report carries nothing here and
is byte-identical to its pre-S24 form. Control *coverage* (what the defender reported
seeing) is not here: it needs the SIEM's alerts, which arrive after the scan, so it
lives in the defender report (``arachne purple report``).
DetectionValidation.title: DetectionValidation

ExecutiveSummary.description: Section 2: narrative, counts and priority order.
ExecutiveSummary.title: ExecutiveSummary

FalsePositiveEntry.description: A finding the analyzer dropped or merged, kept for the appendix (F-05-07).
FalsePositiveEntry.title: FalsePositiveEntry

FeedFreshness.description:
One feed kind's freshness, as the report shows it (REQ-INTEL-001).

``imported_at=None`` means "this deployment has not ingested this feed", which is a
different statement from "the feed is stale" and is rendered as such: a report reader
must be able to tell "we looked and found nothing" from "we never looked".
``severity_contributing`` (WP-21, REQ-INTEL-006) marks the kinds whose staleness moves a
finding's severity, so a reader can weigh a stale timestamp accordingly.
FeedFreshness.title: FeedFreshness

FindingProof.description:
The per-finding proof artifact (S15, REQ-PROOF-013).

Carries what the ladder did to prove this finding — the level, the method, the
token/nonce when the proof was out-of-band or a command echo, and the cleanup
status in operator-readable form. Rendered as the finding's *Proof* section.
FindingProof.title: FindingProof

FrameworkCoverage.description:
One framework's coverage as this scan assessed it (S22, REQ-TRUST-001).

``total_controls`` is the *framework's own* control count (CIS v8.1's 153
safeguards, PCI DSS v4.0's 12 requirements, ISO 27001:2022's 93 Annex A
controls, NIST CSF 2.0's 106 subcategories). ``mapped`` is how many of them
ARACHNE's check catalogue can speak to — of which a scan may still have run
none, which the per-control ``gap`` states. The difference between ``mapped``
and ``total_controls`` is the explicit gap: a report that showed only the mapped
controls would read as coverage it does not have.
FrameworkCoverage.title: FrameworkCoverage

IntelFreshness.description:
The threat-intel block: what data this scan's conclusions rest on (S18).

``stale`` means *an ingested feed is older than its configured TTL*; ``missing`` lists the
kinds nobody ingested. ``providers`` names the third-party indexes the deployment was
allowed to consult (never a key, never a query) so an absent finding from an opted-out
provider is not read as a clean result.

``severity_feeds``/``warnings`` are WP-21's SLA half (REQ-INTEL-006): which kinds move
severity, and one human-readable warning per such kind that is past its SLA. The list is
empty when nothing is stale, which is the ordinary case and keeps a healthy report's
metadata unchanged in substance. A warning is never an error: the report is still valid
and the scan still completed.
IntelFreshness.title: IntelFreshness

Provenance.description: Which engine decided this finding, and on what corpus (F-03-05).
Provenance.title: Provenance

RemediationPlan.description: A resolved catalog entry: summary, steps, verification, refs.
RemediationPlan.title: RemediationPlan

ReportDiff.description:
The scan-to-scan skeleton of F-06-05.

Full trend rendering is S11; this is the data the diff section is written from and the
payload persisted in ``scans_diff``.
ReportDiff.title: ReportDiff

ReportEvidence.description: One evidence payload, addressed by its report id (appendix A).
ReportEvidence.title: ReportEvidence

ReportFinding.description: One finding, exactly the report schema.
ReportFinding.title: ReportFinding

ResidueAttestation.description:
The scan's signed (or explicitly unsigned) residue attestation (WP-14).

``clean`` is the verdict the report and the scan state key on: it is false whenever
``residue`` is non-zero, and the renderers show a warning then. There is no ``None``
reading that means "clean" — a report built without an attestation says so rather than
implying the scan left nothing behind (:func:`arachne.proof.residue.attestation_is_clean`).
ResidueAttestation.title: ResidueAttestation

ResidueEntry.description:
One state change as the residue attestation states it (WP-14, REQ-PROOF-017).

The before-value is a **hash**, never the value: the attestation is an artefact meant to
be handed to a third party, and a target's prior row content is not theirs to read.
ResidueEntry.title: ResidueEntry

ScopeMethodology.description: Section 3: what was scanned, how, and under which limits.
ScopeMethodology.title: ScopeMethodology

Score.description: The F-05-04 scoring output as the report prints it (``score``).
Score.title: Score

SimulatedChange.description: The before/after of a proposed change (S28, REQ-SIM-005).
SimulatedChange.title: SimulatedChange

SimulatedHop.description:
One hop of a simulated path, with its origin stated rather than implied (S28).

``origin`` is the field that keeps a what-if result honest: ``observed`` means a scan
established the hop, ``hypothetical`` means a hypothesis introduced it and
``hypothesis_id`` names which. There is deliberately no ``verified`` field here — the
simulated block's vocabulary must not borrow the verified report's, because a reader
skimming for "verified" inside a what-if section would be reading a claim about a target
that was never touched.
SimulatedHop.title: SimulatedHop

SimulatedPathEntry.description: One path composed inside a simulation (S28, REQ-SIM-002).
SimulatedPathEntry.title: SimulatedPathEntry

SimulationBlock.description:
A what-if run's result, rendered in its own section (S28, REQ-SIM-002/004).

The block is **optional** and never populated by a scan: it is attached when an operator
asks for a simulation of a stored scan (``arachne report --simulate``). That is what keeps
an ordinary report byte-identical to its pre-S28 form, and what makes the separation
structural rather than a rendering convention — the paths here live in a field no
finding-shaped consumer reads.

disclosure.default: Nothing in this section was observed on a target. It is a computation over the estate model built from earlier scans, under the hypothetical states listed below.
disclosure.title: Disclosure

SimulationBlock.title: SimulationBlock

SimulationHypothesis.description: One hypothetical state a run injected, as the report shows it (S28).
SimulationHypothesis.title: SimulationHypothesis

StateChangeEntry.description:
One L4 state change, for the report-level *state changes* table (REQ-PROOF-013).

``restored=False`` is not a rendering detail — it is a repair instruction: the
target is not in its prior state and an operator must act (REQ-PROOF-010).
StateChangeEntry.title: StateChangeEntry

Timestamps.description: When the finding was first and last seen, and when it was verified.
Timestamps.title: Timestamps

VerificationRecord.description:
How one finding was established (WP-13, REQ-PROOF-015/016).

The durable counterpart of the proof ladder's act: the rung used, the method, the
observations that established it, a reproducibility token, when, and which version of
the check did it. ``status`` is ``verified`` when a check's own evidence established the
claim and ``unverified`` when the report has no record to show — in which case the
finding is forced to ``info`` (see :class:`ReportFinding`). ``parent_record_id`` links a
re-verification to the record it re-checked and ``outcome`` says what the re-run found.
VerificationRecord.title: VerificationRecord
